text:
alex: Heads-up: we saw a sustained p99 jump (from ~120ms to ~350ms) on a dedicated pool this morning during long-context jobs. Appears correlated with KV cache paging -> eviction churn under heavy mixed-length traffic. :eyes:

jia: Which eviction policy was on that pool? LRU or FIFO?

alex: LRU. We flipped a token evict heuristic last week that tries to favour older KV pages for eviction under bursty small-seq workloads. Suspect that interacts badly with our batching heuristics.

maria: That change was the one that pins recent KV segments for 2x the normal window so micro-batching doesn't thrash the cache, right?

alex: Exactly. It reduces recompute for small batches but under sustained long-context tails it causes fragmentation. When the heap gets tight we start paging whole pages out -> eviction storms.

ryan: Do we have a reproducer? Can we run a synthetic that mixes long (8k) and short (128) sequences to trigger the pattern?

alex: Yes. Quick repro I used locally:```bash
# hammer long/short mix
for i in {1..200}; do
  if (( i % 5 == 0 )); then
    curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"seq_len":8000}' >/dev/null &
  else
    curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"seq_len":128}' >/dev/null &
  fi
done
wait
```
Run it against a single-worker dedicated image with KV debug on. It reliably pushes p99 up after ~90s.

jia: Nice. Any profiler output? flamegraph or heap dump?

alex: I attached the flame-ish summary snippet from perf on the hot worker (trimmed):
```
47%  runtime  [kernel.kallsyms]  page_fault_handler
18%  infer_srv  kv_cache::evict_pages
12%  infer_srv  batching::coalesce_requests
6%   infer_srv  kv_cache::apply_reuse_map
```
The page_fault_handler shows up because we start faulting into swapped pages when the allocator hits the high watermark. eviction routine CPU is non-trivial too.

maria: Hmm. Does LRU correctness hold when we do deferred reuse? We had a bug where reuse_map entries pointed at old offsets after a compaction pass. Could that explain wrong cache hits -> extra recompute?

alex: I instrumented a counter: "evict_then_reuse_mismatch" — it increments when a reuse_map lookup returns a segment that was previously evicted this cycle. It increments about 5-10k times in the repro. So there's definitely a race where evicted segments are still referenced by in-flight batches.

ryan: That sounds like a correctness issue, not just policy tuning. If an in-flight request references a segment that got paged out and then reallocated, we could be returning wrong KV context or crashing. Any examples of corrupted outputs?

alex: We saw occasional context drift in long chats (tokens repeating earlier prompts). Not consistent but correlates with the mismatch counter spikes.

jia: Ok we need triage plan. My proposed steps:
1) Add a brief stop-the-world check to the eviction path: mark segments "evict-pending" and ensure in-flight refs hold a refcount before reclaiming. If refcount > 0 then skip.
2) Add a smaller microbenchmark to reproduce the race deterministically (control timing between batch apply and eviction).
3) Run with FIFO policy variant to compare throughput/latency under same load.

maria: I can wire step 1 quickly. Also want to log which segment offsets are being reclaimed when mismatch counter ticks. That'll let us correlate to request ids.

perf-bot: perf report uploaded: https://perf.internal/redwood/reports/1775001234-kv-evict-run.html

alex: After adding a simple refcount guard locally, p99 drops back near baseline and the mismatch counter goes to zero under the same repro. So it's definitely a race. But we still see more eviction activity than expected; policy is still brittle under memory pressure.

ryan: Interesting. How does FIFO behave? Did you test switching the pool to FIFO?

alex: I ran FIFO variant in the same env. Latency profile changes: median is slightly worse (~10%), but p99 is more stable — fewer spikes. FIFO avoids keeping tiny hot fragments around, which reduces fragmentation-induced paging.

maria: That suggests a hybrid strategy might work: prefer LRU for short-window workloads, but if eviction rate crosses threshold, switch to FIFO or increase page-size coalescing.

jia: Also check kernel selection: we've been switching to a memory-optimized kernel that reduces working set per token, but it increases per-batch scheduling jitter. The jitter exacerbates in-flight ref timings, making the race more likely.

alex: Good call. When I forced the throughput-optimized kernel instead, the scheduling jitter drops and the mismatch frequency halves. So kernel choice + batching heuristics affect correctness windows, not just raw perf.

sre-oncall: For prod mitigation I recommend two short-term actions: 1) enable the refcount guard across Dedicated pools, 2) auto-fallback to FIFO when eviction-rate > 100 pages/sec for 30s. That buys time while we implement a robust GC/compaction strategy.

maria: Agreed. I'll open a PR for the refcount guard + logs. Jia, can you own the FIFO auto-fallback experiment? We should A/B it on a small customer pool first.

jia: Yep will run A/B tomorrow. I'll also add a microprofile hook to record per-request KV refs and eviction decisions (low-overhead sampling).

alex: I'll follow up with a writeup of the flame/perf traces and the small repro script. If folks want to reproduce locally, use the repro above + set ENV KV_DEBUG=1 and KV_PAGE_SIZE=64MB.

ryan: Awesome. Thanks for the fast triage. Once PRs land let's schedule a short postmortem and update the runbook for eviction storms. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks team — saved a few customers from jitter this morning. We'll paste links here when PRs and results are in.

maria: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/kv-cache/pull/412 — draft, includes logs and tests for evict/reuse races.

jia: Experiment plan doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/kv-fallback-ab-test.md

alex: Adding to runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/eviction-storms.md — will include the quick mitigation steps.

sre-oncall: Will monitor the canary and escalate if error-rate or p99 exceed thresholds.

alex: cc @ryan @maria @jia — I'll post the perf flame link and heap snapshots once uploaded.
